question: The governor of a province (bhukti) in the Pala and Pratihara empire was called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uparika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Uparika** was used to designate the **governor of a province (bhukti)** during the **Pala and Pratihara empire**.
 
• In ancient India, provinces or large administrative units were known as **bhuktis**, and the Uparika was responsible for overseeing the administration within these provinces.
 
• The Uparika was generally appointed by the central authority, such as the king or emperor, to ensure proper governance and collection of revenue in the bhukti.
 
• During the reign of the **Pala dynasty**, the administrative structure was highly centralized, and the Uparika played a crucial role in maintaining order and implementing policies at the provincial level.
 
• The **Pratihara empire**, known for its vast territorial expanse, required efficient provincial governance, which was carried out by officials like the Uparika.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Administrative Structure in the Pala and Pratihara Empires:**

 
 
• The Pala empire (8th to 12th century CE) was known for its centralized administrative system, with the king at the apex and officials like **Uparika** managing provinces.
 
• The Pratihara empire (8th to 11th century CE) had a similar structure, with provinces being governed by Uparikas to ensure smooth administration.
 
• Both empires employed a system of revenue collection, and the Uparikas played a key role in ensuring the proper functioning of this system at the provincial level.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Uparika:**
 
 
• Uparika was tasked with maintaining law and order within the province.
 
• He ensured the efficient collection of taxes and revenues from the bhukti and its smaller administrative units, known as **visayas**.
 
• He implemented the policies and orders issued by the central government or the king.
 
• Uparika also oversaw judicial functions and resolved disputes at the provincial level.
 
 
 
• **Other Administrative Titles:**
 
 
• **Rashtrapati:** This term referred to the head of a **Rashtra** (a larger administrative unit), but it was not used for provincial governors in the Pala and Pratihara empires.
 
• **Visayapati:** This title was given to the official in charge of a **visaya** (district or smaller administrative unit).
 
• **Koshtapala:** This term was associated with treasury officials and not the provincial governors.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Pala dynasty ruled over regions of **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha**, while the Pratiharas controlled much of northern India during their reign.
 
• Effective provincial administration was vital for maintaining the vast territories under these empires, and the Uparikas played a significant role in this regard.
 
• These administrative practices set the groundwork for later governance systems in medieval India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bhukti:** Refers to a province or large territorial division within the empire, governed by the Uparika.
 
• **Visayas:** Smaller administrative units within a Bhukti, managed by Visayapatis under the supervision of the Uparika.
 
• **Revenue Collection:** The Uparika ensured the efficient collection of taxes, which were vital for the empire's economy and governance.
 
• **Centralized Administration:** Both the Pala and Pratihara empires relied on centralized governance, with provincial governors ensuring the implementation of policies.
 
• **Judicial Responsibilities:** The Uparika also played a role in resolving disputes and maintaining justice within the province.
